results.prompt: Who is Kevin Rajan (kvnloo)? What is he known for publicly?
results.stdout:
Kevin Rajan, online as `kvnloo`, is a Chicago-based software builder who publicly describes himself as the solo founder of **zer0**. His public profile emphasizes autonomous systems, AI-assisted engineering, human performance, and making software creation more accessible.

Publicly, he is primarily known for:

- **AI agents and autonomous development tooling**
  - **evolve** — a multi-agent development and orchestration framework
  - **tmux-agent-fleet** — a daemon-free command palette for coordinating coding agents across tmux panes
  - Public zer0 components for agent orchestration, progress monitoring, provider adapters, and local voice interaction

- **Interactive 3D applications and simulations**
  - **ace** — a digital-twin demo of an autonomous multi-floor racket-sports facility
  - **monument** — a Monument Valley–style WebGL demo and AI game-design workbench
  - **portfolio / Kevin’s Ramen & Boba** — an interactive 3D presentation of his public projects
  - Other public experiments span Three.js, WebGL, digital twins, procedural scenes, and game-like interfaces

- **Human-performance, neuroscience, audio, and mobile experiments**
  - **FlowState** — an EEG/BCI experiment that adjusts video playback speed using alpha-band attention
  - **AudioEngine** — a 2017 iOS real-time noise meter and 14-band dual-channel equalizer
  - Earlier Swift/iOS projects including smart-wearable concepts and course applications

- **Building in public**
  - **boplog** is his canonical chronological archive of repositories to which he has actually committed, rather than every repository or fork appearing on his GitHub account.
  - As of its July 31, 2026 refresh, the archive reports **52 public projects**, **13 products**, and coverage from **2017–2026**.

The most accurate concise description is:

> Kevin Rajan (`kvnloo`) is a software builder and solo founder of zer0 whose public work centers on autonomous AI development systems, agent tooling, interactive 3D simulations, and human-performance technology.

This characterization comes mainly from his own public work and self-description; it should not be read as evidence of private projects, funding, company size, or unpublished accomplishments.

Sources:

- Canonical build log: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/
- Machine-readable overview: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/llms.txt
- Public project manifest: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/data/manifest.json
- GitHub: https://github.com/kvnloo
- Portfolio: https://kvnloo.github.io/portfolio/

In short, evolve is a toolkit and product track for coordinating swarms of coding agents toward end-to-end autonomous software development. This describes only its documented public scope; it does not imply private capabilities or unpublished plans.

tmux-agent-fleet is an open-source tmux plugin by Kevin Rajan (`kvnloo`) that provides a fast, searchable command palette for coding-agent sessions across tmux panes.

Pressing `prefix + f` opens an `fzf` dashboard that can:

- Discover live agents from tmux process metadata—no daemon or hooks required
- Recognize Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, Grok, Oh My Pi, Pi, and Fable
- Show ordinary shells, REPLs, and servers too
- Preview a selected pane’s live output
- Jump directly to the selected pane
- Optionally include Agent Deck sessions
- Use pywal colors or its built-in theme

It is intentionally a switcher and monitor, not an orchestrator: it does not manage worktrees, inject commands, install agent hooks, collect transcripts, or send telemetry.

The canonical boplog record classifies it as a featured 2026 Shell project under `zer0 → product → agent tooling`, dated July 14, 2026. It requires tmux 3.2+, Bash 4+, and `fzf`, and is MIT-licensed.

Sources:
- Canonical build log: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/
- Public project record: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/data/projects-2026.json
- Repository and installation instructions: https://github.com/kvnloo/tmux-agent-fleet
